state.timeline: A single current-policy source provides linearizable reads and strictly increasing non-reusable positions for every policy change. A first read at time 1 returns V1 at position 4. Time T is 2. A second read at time 3 returns position 4. All conditions are established, not assumed from the aggregate implementation.
state.changed: A current-policy source returns V1 at position 4 on the first qualified read. Policy V2 commits before T and advances the position to 5. The qualified second read after T returns position 5.
state.stale: A node reads a lagging cache twice and sees V1 both times. V2 may already have committed before either cache read. No freshness or lineage guarantee is available.

same_through_t.instructions: In timeline, can the policy have changed at or before T after the first read without changing the position returned by the second read?

current_at_t.instructions: In timeline, was V1 the current policy at T?

changed_equal.instructions: In changed, are the first and second positions equal?

stale_proves.instructions: In stale, do two matching cache reads prove V1 remained current at T?
